in_vocabulary.measurement: R_phi val gain, 4 seeds per arm, identical data and capacity

sign_across_4_seeds.x2: 4/4 negative but |delta| 0.000-0.030, at the edge of resolution
sign_across_4_seeds.deblur: 4/4 negative at -0.144/-0.099/-0.102/-0.092 -> a real, consistent deficit

in_vocabulary.caveat: the big sets hold 10351-13672 per operator and were never used for this comparison; a sweep is running because a 17-dim condition is more data-hungry than a 6-dim one

mis_conditioning_control.setup: x4 input, x6 descriptor, same 53 clips, paired against the x4 descriptor
mis_conditioning_control.reading: handing the arm the WRONG operator costs the same as the entire mtf-vs-onehot difference, so this metric has no resolving power for the conditioning signal. The innerDC projection onto R_phi(y) absorbs it. Conditioning must be judged at the R_phi level, not after the DiT.

deblur_conditioning_was_never_implemente.bug: mtf_cond caches on the operator STRING; every deblur sample passed the bare 'deblur' and operator_desc fell back to its default sigma=1.75, so one constant vector covered a kernel range of sigma 1.0-2.5

cannot_be_fixed_at_inference.reading: the network bound that constant as the identity of "deblur"; a retrain was required to test the idea at all

after_retraining_with_per_sample_kernels.flag: --mtf-persample (opt-in, so every earlier number stays reproducible)
after_retraining_with_per_sample_kernels.per_sigma_bin: one-hot leads in every bin; its lead shrinks as sigma grows (0.079 -> 0.011)
after_retraining_with_per_sample_kernels.verdict: the fix is real and directionally right, but within the seed spread and still behind one-hot. The deblur column is a negative result, not an implementation note -- which is only knowable because the implementation was fixed first.

the_boundary.principle: MTF generalises to an operator it never trained on when the descriptor lands among trained operators that share a behaviour; it collapses when the bracketing operators behave incompatibly, and distance alone does not predict which

bracketed_by: denoise (MTF all ones, nothing to restore)
x2 (restore three quarters of the spectrum)
deblur_sigma_0.5_0.9.reading: flat across bins rather than graded by distance, which is what "the condition selects an incompatible behaviour" predicts

the_boundary.why_distance_is_not_the_criterion: deblur:0.9 sits at L2 0.139, closer than x6 at 0.207, and still collapses
the_boundary.why_the_direction_is_asymmetric: an MTF is bounded in [0,1]: sigma 1.0->0.5 moves it 1.30 in L2 toward all-ones, while sigma 2.5->3.5 moves it only 0.24 toward all-zeros. The physical parameter does not reveal which extrapolation is cheap.
the_boundary.checkable_before_deployment: compute the descriptor from the operator alone, take its distance to the trained set and read the nearest neighbours; no image is involved, so this stays inside the non-blind setting

what_this_means_for_the_claim.where_mtf_demonstrably_helps: at the R_phi level on operators outside the vocabulary: x6 +2.088 dB and x3 +7.586 dB where a one-hot raises SystemExit, and 52.0%% of the bicubic LPIPS gap filled at the pixel level on x6 against 53.0%% for a trained x4
what_this_means_for_the_claim.where_it_does_not: at deployment. Three independent measurements agree: mis-conditioning with the wrong operator costs +0.0009 LPIPS, mtf-vs-onehot is +0.0008, and swapping an assumed descriptor for a measured one is -0.0007. The innerDC projection onto R_phi(y) and the DiT prior absorb the difference.
what_this_means_for_the_claim.honest_framing: MTF conditioning buys REPRESENTABILITY, not accuracy. It makes operators runnable that a one-hot cannot express, and that is checkable before deployment from the operator alone. It does not make the delivered video measurably better on operators either signal can express.

limits: the boundary principle is supported by four operator families (x6, x3, two deblur ranges), not proven; it predicts the sign of every case measured so far but has not been tested on an operator bracketed by same-behaviour trainers at LARGE descriptor distance
all conditioning comparisons are at 590 training windows per operator; the 3000-window sweep is running and the 10351-window point is not done
the x6 and x3 numbers are R_phi-level PSNR; the pixel-level x6 table is being judged separately on data/real_eval/heldout_s6
x3 has only 22 training windows available in its pair set, so its val n is 6 -- the +7.586 dB is indicative, not a measurement at the same weight as x6

does_the_descriptor_matter_at_deployment.question: On real degradation, does feeding the MEASURED transfer function instead of the assumed x4 one change anything? Same checkpoint (omni_mtf_k3), same clips, only the descriptor differs.
does_the_descriptor_matter_at_deployment.why_three_arms: op uses operator_mtf(4) on a white-noise probe; control uses a synthetic x4 pair measured on the same natural frames; measured uses the real lens measured the same way. control exists because the same x4 operator differs by L2 1.02 between the two conventions -- without it, a measured-vs-op gap is unattributable.
does_the_descriptor_matter_at_deployment.result: the operator effect is -0.0007 LPIPS with sd 0.0029 and wins on 7 of 15 clips, i.e. nothing. The convention effect is +0.0051, seven times larger. Replacing an assumed descriptor with the measured one -- an L2 of 0.53-0.92 apart -- does not change the output.
does_the_descriptor_matter_at_deployment.retracts: the pre-registered prediction that conditioning would FAIL here because the measured MTF is non-monotone. It does not fail; it does not act at all. The prediction was also untestable as first run, because that run used r5_k3, whose cfg has desc:false.
does_the_descriptor_matter_at_deployment.and_the_control_earned_its_place: with only op and measured, the +0.0044 total would have been reported as evidence that the operator assumption is wrong. Almost all of it is the measurement convention. This is the same error shape as reading psnr_gtrange on a set whose operator is not x4 bicubic.

unconditioned_arm_is_best_here.reading: on real degradation the single-operator estimator with no descriptor at all edges out every conditioned arm, which is consistent with the shipped configuration
